# Spec card: Mixed review — a seeded, sendable mix of skills from any grades and areas (new page type, PAGE_TYPES 5.5 proposed)

Written by hand from `design/cards/mixed-review/card.json` in the structure `ws-spec-card.mjs` generates (nine sections, the Signed line, the informational §7b). Builders read this card; critics keep reading the full standards and `design/audit/RUBRIC.md`. Keep card.json and this file in step.

A new page type that is a **configuration of the mixed-practice engine, not a second engine**. A pure pool / deal module turns the teacher's filters (grades, areas, only 8/10, unticked skills, from my lessons) and a seed into an explicit list of N items `{categoryId, skillId, opts, seed}`. `buildSheet` lays that list out with `sheet/roles/mixed-practice.js` in review mode (the supports rule of `sheet/roles/review.js`). Every screen host plays the same list. A share code carries the list, the counts, the order, the seed and the size, so the mix is reproduced exactly.

**The deal is executable, not prose (card round 3, root cause of r1 and r2).** `design/cards/mixed-review/proto/dealer-v1.mjs` is DEALER V1: a pure ES module (no DOM, no `window`, no `Math.random`) that turns the pool, the filters, N, the seed, the order, the size (M / L), the week and day and the optional adapt weights into the dealt items, the page split, the shelves and the week. It NEVER measures a page: the split comes from a frozen size × footprint table. `proto/check-v1.mjs` proves every rule of §2, §3 and §7a on pinned fixtures (`node design/cards/mixed-review/proto/check-v1.mjs` → `check-v1: OK (15 props, 50 fixtures; trace 117 normative sentences, 84 by a property, 33 by a product check)`), and the §3 table is printed by `check-v1.mjs --table`. Where this card and the prototype differ, the prototype is right and the card is the defect. The product dealer is that file moved, unchanged, to `js/modules/mixed-review.js` (§9b step 2).

| Piece | Where | New? |
|---|---|---|
| Layout, shelves, interleave, numbering | `js/modules/sheet/roles/mixed-practice.js`, `js/modules/sheet/interleave.js` (`dealCounts`, `interleave`) | extended (inputs `total`, `review`, `order`) |
| Supports at review level | `js/modules/sheet/roles/review.js` rule PT-REV-2 (level 1, no steps / models / traces) | read, not changed |
| Key and key summary | `js/modules/sheet/roles/answer-key.js` (`renderAnswerKey`, `answerListRows`, `skillItemMap`) | extended (summary, weekly table) |
| Request and role routing | `js/modules/print-sheet.js` `buildSheet`; `js/modules/sheet/roles/index.js` `ROLE_ALIASES` | alias `mixed-review` |
| Pool, deal, pages, shelves, week, weights, code | `js/modules/mixed-review.js` = `design/cards/mixed-review/proto/dealer-v1.mjs` moved unchanged | NEW, pure (no DOM, no `Math.random`); plans pages from a frozen table, never measures |
| Areas, grades, ✓ list | `teacher-areas.js` `areaOf` / `AREA_ORDER` / `AREAS` + the NEW `AREA_LABELS` export (built here, §9.1); `wrm-links.js` (pacing, `weekForDate`); `redesign-passed.js` `REDESIGN_PASSED` | read |

## 1. What it teaches

Retrieval of skills already taught: a short sheet of 5 to 30 problems drawn from the grades and maths areas the teacher ticks, each problem in its own skill's cell at review supports (PT-REV-2), numbered 1..N, scored, with a facsimile answer key and a key summary by area and skill. On screen the same N problems play as a practice card, an online worksheet, a scored quiz and the boss / race games.

**Skills on this page type:** none of its own. Any live skill the filters admit (§7). It adds no skill, no preset, no `SKILL_STANDARDS` / `SKILL_WRM` tag (§9.12). Today the only-8/10 pool is **32 skills** (from `redesign-passed.js`, 2026-11-19): K 4 (OA), 1: 9 (OA 7, NBT 2), 2: 10 (NBT), 3: 4 (NBT 1, OA 3), 4: 1 (NBT), 5: 2 (NBT), M: 2 (Words); areas OA, NBT and Words only — so only-8/10 defaults OFF (§9.6).

**Research.** No premium logins this round (the card writer has no browser). From knowledge of the reference sites: MathWorksheets4Kids mixed / spiral review grade packs (a fixed mix of 10–20 items across strands a page, an answer key); K5 Learning mixed-operations and grade review sheets; IXL recommendations and skill plans (screen-side choice of weak skills, a per-skill score report); Math-Drills mixed sheets with a seeded "new set". Converted to our design: 6–12 problems a page, not 30–50 (12.1); one boxed cell per problem in its own skill's cell; numbers, not letters (PT-MIX-7); the pupil page never names the area (§9.13). **Lane MR-B repeats the research with the logins before it builds** (CLAUDE.md, mandatory).

## 2. Problem types and progression

- No new problem type: each item is its own skill's cell at level 1 (PT-REV-2) with its own instruction in the cell or in its band strip (PT-MIX-4, PT-MIX-5).
- **The mix is DEALER V1** (`proto/dealer-v1.mjs`). Each rule sentence carries a property tag (the letter P, a colon and the `check-v1` property, in square brackets) naming the property that asserts it; `check-v1.mjs --trace` fails on a rule sentence of §2, §3, §7a or PT-MXR with no tag, or with a tag naming no property (§9e). Where §2 and the prototype differ, the prototype is right and §2 is the defect.
  1. **Pool.** The pool is `filterPool(pool, filters)` (§7a), and MIXED and NOSTD skills never enter it [P:n]. A pool under 2 skills is refused with its reason, never dealt or widened (§9.6) [P:n].
  2. **Classes, from a frozen table.** A registry row names its footprint `kind`; V1 reads the class from its frozen `KIND_CLASS`, which has a row for each of the 10 `StaticFootprint` kinds of SKILL_CELL_CONTRACT 3.5: fact and equation compact; stack, visual-half, table, text and legacy typical; visual-full, division (long division) and word-problem wide [P:h]. A word-problem skill holds at most 3 items a page at M and at L (12.1 plain rows; `KIND_CAP`) [P:h].
  3. **Pages from the frozen table, never measured.** `CAP[size][class]` is M compact 12, typical 12, wide 4 and L compact 10, typical 8, wide 3 (12.1) [P:h]. For a one-class pool the pages are exactly the §3 table, `pageSize(R, C) = ceil(R / ceil(R / C))`, largest page first [P:h]. No page fills more than one page, where fill = Σ count / cap of the skill's class (a wide item at M is a quarter page) [P:h]. No page holds more than 7 shelves at M or 5 at L [P:h].
  4. **Skills a page.** A page holds at most 3 distinct skills [P:c]. No skill holds more than ceil(N / 2) items on the sheet [P:b]. A flat (compact or typical) skill always holds at least 2 items on every page it is on, with no exception [P:j2]. A wide skill may hold 1 (a wide shelf of 1) [P:j2].
  5. **Fill.** Every page but a sheet's last is at least half full [P:k]. The last page may be under half full, because the teacher chose N (§9.18) [P:k]. No page holds fewer than 2 items, the last page included [P:l].
  6. **Exact N.** Exactly N items, numbered 1..N row-major over the pages, and the pages' shelves hold exactly N cells [P:e].
  7. **Item seeds.** Item i (0-based) of a sheet has seed `deriveSeed('mixed-review', S′, day, i)`, four parts, where S′ = S and day = 0 on a single sheet, and S′ = the day seed `deriveSeed('mixed-review-week', S, d)` and day = d on day d of a week [P:m,f].
  8. **Determinism.** The same input always gives the same plan, and a code decoded and re-dealt gives the identical items, seeds, options and pages [P:a].
- **How V1 chooses** (the mechanics; the code is the specification, and the promises are the rules above). The cycle is `shuffle(rng(deriveSeed('mixed-review-cycle', S)), pool)`; a replayed code uses the code's list in its order with no shuffle; adapt uses a weighted seeded order of the code's listed skills (§7a Weighting). Each page opens with the first skill in the choice order (fresh to the sheet, and in a week fresh to the week, then not on yesterday's sheet, then least used on this sheet and this week, then pick order) and takes up to max(1, min(3, floor(n_p / 2))) skills of its group (wide or flat); `dealCounts` (interleave.js; equal weights, min 2) splits n_p over them, lowest sheet totals first; a count over its skill's room moves to the skill with the most room. A page under half full while items remain is topped up by fill with skills of either class (lead ruling 2026-11-20, §9.18), each taking at least 2 items if flat [P:k,j2]. A page that would leave a flat skill exactly one item of room takes that item now or leaves one more; a page that would leave exactly 1 item to deal takes one more, or adds one item of a new wide skill, or gives one back [P:j2,l]. A last page under half full joins the latest earlier page it fits beside (fill ≤ 1, at most 3 skills, the shelf ceiling kept); counts do not change in the merge [P:c,h]. `check-v1.mjs --fill` runs props k, l and j2 over 10 pools × every N × M, L × the 3 orders × 300 seeds, plus 40 weeks a cell: 0 pages break them [P:k,l,j2].
- **Order** (the teacher's choice; §7a Order modes):
  - `mixed` (default): on a page whose skills are all one class and none is a legacy cell, the M1 arrangement (the items interleaved by the real `interleave`, maxRun 1, rows of k cells); on any other page, GROUPED shelves of one skill in a seeded `interleave`d order (`deriveSeed('mixed-review-page', S, day, p)`). A legacy cell is never in the M1 arrangement (`mixedClass` refuses it) [P:j]. On every page there is no AVOIDABLE adjacent pair of one skill: the adjacent same-skill pairs equal the fewest the counts allow, max(0, 2·major − T − 1); a single-skill page is exempt, because its shelves are necessarily side by side (§9.17 r2 resolution 1) [P:d]. The screen plays the printed order [X:MIX-REVIEW-HOSTS].
  - `easyhard`: the shelves of every page run by placement grade, K to 6+ (M last), then pick order [P:d].
  - `area`: the shelves of every page run in `AREA_ORDER` (CC, OA, NBT, NF, MEAS, DATA, G, RPNS, WORDS), then by grade [P:d].

## 3. The drawing

- **Sizes M and L only** (owner 2026-11-13; S dropped: a stored S or an S code reads as M through `offeredSize`) [X:ws-no-size-s]. Look **Daily** (mixed-practice `DEFAULT_LOOK`); lattice Auto N = 6 at M, 4 at L. Shelves: at most **7 at M, 5 at L** a page (12.1 Mixed practice) [P:h]. Problems a page: at most **12 at M, 10 at L** (12.1 Review 12 / 8–12; DN-1: never over 20 at L), at most **4 at M, 3 at L** when the page's items are wide visuals (12.1 Wide-visual rows: number lines, base-10 over 100, coin rows), and at most 3 word problems at M and at L [P:h]. **At most 3 distinct skills a page** (12.1 Review: 2–3 instruction-led sections) [P:c].
- **Supports:** level 1 for every item, as a Review (PT-REV-2): structural scaffolds stay; hint scaffolds, steps, models and traces do not appear, and there are no anchors [X:MIX-REVIEW-COUNT].
- **Header:** Name · Date · Score ___ / N; two-line tab `Level <grades> | Review` (a week: `Week n | Mon`); title `Mixed review` (HD-13). Footer: the plain CCSS codes of the dealt skills (PT-MIX-7) and, on the teacher footer line, the code and seed.
- **Body:** shelves of one skill each (`SHELF[size][class]` cells: M compact 3, typical 3, wide 1; L compact 4, typical 2, wide 1; a divisor of the Auto lattice), each opening with its band strip (the skill's own instruction, no skill title, no area name), in the order of §2; or, on a one-class page with no legacy cell, the M1 mixed arrangement (one "Solve." strip, each cell keeps its own instruction) [X:MIX-REVIEW-COUNT]. A shelf never holds more than its k cells, and a short shelf is only ever a skill's last [P:j]. Numbering runs 1..N row-major across pages [P:e]. No in-cell skill letter prints (PT-MIX-7) [X:MIX-REVIEW-COUNT].
- **SHELF k equals the passed geometry.** The frozen k of each class at M and L must equal the k that `mixed-practice.js` draws for a passed skill of that class (`factPick` / the M1 lattice); a release that draws another k fails MIX-REVIEW-COUNT `count-shelf-k-differs` (browser, build step 1), and the engine then draws V1's k within DN-10, never re-plans [X:MIX-REVIEW-COUNT].
- **Key:** the facsimile pages (PT-KEY-1), then the **key summary** (§7a breakdown).

**Capacity / density** — GENERATED by `node design/cards/mixed-review/proto/check-v1.mjs --table` from the frozen `CAP` table of DEALER V1 (A4, full header; a one-class pool). The page split is the dealer's, not the engine's: the engine draws the plan and never re-plans it (L16) [X:MIX-REVIEW-COUNT]. The dealer's pages equal this table at M and L for every N, and `fixtures/size-table.json` pins it [P:h].

| N | M compact / typical (12) | M wide (4) | L compact (10) | L typical (8) | L wide (3) |
|--:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 1 (2-up: 5 and 5) | 2 (3 + 2) | 1 (2-up: 5 and 5) | 1 (5) | 2 (3 + 2) |
| 10 | 1 (10) | 3 (4 + 3 + 3) | 1 (10) | 2 (5 + 5) | 4 (3 + 3 + 2 + 2) |
| 15 | 2 (8 + 7) | 4 (4 + 4 + 4 + 3) | 2 (8 + 7) | 2 (8 + 7) | 5 (3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3) |
| 20 | 2 (10 + 10) | 5 (4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4) | 2 (10 + 10) | 3 (7 + 7 + 6) | 7 (3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 2) |
| 25 | 3 (9 + 8 + 8) | 7 (4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 3 + 3) | 3 (9 + 8 + 8) | 4 (7 + 6 + 6 + 6) | 9 (3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 2) |
| 30 | 3 (10 + 10 + 10) | 8 (4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 3) | 3 (10 + 10 + 10) | 4 (8 + 8 + 7 + 7) | 10 (3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3) |

- Skills on a sheet: Σ s_p over its pages when the pool is large enough (a page of 2–3 items holds 1 skill). A pool of mixed classes opens wide and flat class pages and joins them by fill when a page would be under half full. Every page is within one page's fill [P:h]. Every page but the last is at least half full [P:k]. No page holds a lone item [P:l].
- **A shelf never splits** (PT-MIX-9) [X:MIX-REVIEW-COUNT]. **A skill's last shelf may be short** (r2 resolution 3), and a short shelf is never anything but a skill's last [P:j]. It is drawn left-aligned: its cells keep their own template width and height, and the row simply ends early — no empty frame, no stretched cell, no blank slot [X:ws-empty-band]. H13 allows it: H13 measures empty bands INSIDE cells and rows sized for a taller item, and a short shelf has neither (its row is its cells' height).
- **H5 — lead ruling 2026-11-20 (§9.18), and the lone item (card r3 D2).** (a) The LAST page of an exact-N sheet may be under half full: the teacher chose N [P:k]. (b) Every other page is at least half full: whenever a class page (wide or flat) would be under half full while items remain, V1 tops it up with skills of either class by fill (§2 "How V1 chooses"), so wide and flat items share one page [P:k]. (c) No page, the last included, holds fewer than 2 items: a 1-item last page is never unavoidable, because the page before it can always take one more or give one back (§2 rule 5) [P:l]. `check-v1.mjs --fill` finds 0 non-last pages under half full, 0 one-item pages and 0 one-item flat skills over 10 pinned pools (23-skill, compact, typical, wide, wide + flat 2-skill, wide + compact + typical 3-skill, 2-skill, 6-skill, the 10 kinds, 2 legacy) × every N × M, L × 3 orders × 300 seeds, plus 40 weeks a cell [P:k,l,j2]. Without the guards (`--no-lone-guard`) the 2-skill wide + flat pool leaves one-item pages and is caught (`fail-l-lone-item`, `fail-j2-flat-one`); the old separate-pages dealer is caught by `fail-k-separate-pages`.
- **When a drawn page cannot hold its dealt cells** (a release whose cell is taller than the table assumed), the engine spills whole shelves to a continuation page and keeps the numbering and the deal; it never re-deals (MIX-REVIEW-COUNT `count-spill-redeal`) [X:MIX-REVIEW-COUNT].
- **N = 5 prints 2-up** (§9.7) exactly when the 5 fit a half page (fill ≤ ½: M compact / typical, L compact): the same 5 items twice on one sheet, each half with its own header (Name, Date, Score ___ / 5) and numbered 1–5, a dashed cut line between; the key is 2-up the same way, each half numbered 1–5 [P:e]. Otherwise the table's own pages apply [P:h].
- Key pages = pupil pages + the summary: under the last key page's grid when its rows fit (rows × 7 mm + 14 mm), else one more key page. A week adds one weekly-table page.

## 4. Rules that apply

### 4a. Core rules — apply every one (15 rules; quoted from `design/cards/rule-index.json`)

**The engine it reuses**

- **PT-MIX-4** (PAGE_TYPES) GROUPED packing. Each skill gets one shelf first; further shelves go to the skill with the largest gap between its target share and its achieved share, while they fit. Each shelf uses its own template's minimum height; spare height is shared equally into the answer zones. Each shelf opens with a band strip (bold skill title plus one instruction). *(This card: no skill title on a review band, §9.13.)*
- **PT-MIX-6** (PAGE_TYPES) Skills are dealt by weighted round-robin; in SHUFFLED, runs of the same skill are 2 or fewer.
- **PT-MIX-7** (PAGE_TYPES) Numbering: GROUPED row-major; SHUFFLED by strip, block, then inside the block. No in-cell skill letter prints (it would read as multiple choice); the skill-to-item map lives on the answer key and the footer lists plain CCSS codes.
- **PT-MIX-9** (PAGE_TYPES) A shelf or strip never splits; too many tall skills spill to page 2 with weights re-solved across both pages.
- **PT-REV-2** (PAGE_TYPES) Supports equal those of the last lesson taught. Steps, models and traces do not appear.
- **PT-CMP-1** (PAGE_TYPES) Any skill can appear on any page role. A role never refuses a skill; the skill's `footprint` decides how many items fit, never whether the skill is allowed. What travels into the role is the configured skill …

**Keys, seeds, sharing, pupil data**

- **PT-KEY-1** (PAGE_TYPES) Every page of every role has a key, for every skill; a page with scored cells can never print without one being available. The key is the identical page rendered with `state: answered`: same geometry, same labels, same pagination. The lint checks that the key's cell count equals the pupil page's.
- **PT-KEY-5** (PAGE_TYPES) Mixed Skill Practice keys add the skill-to-item map and per-skill subtotals under the grid. Daily Spiral and Daily 4 may add one weekly table (slots as rows, days as columns). …
- **PT-DLG-21** (PAGE_TYPES) Form and seed … week and day; seed; "new numbers" — form A, random seed stored with the job — the same seed reprints the same page.
- **PT-DLG-26** (PAGE_TYPES) No option, field or page in this model records, stores or charts a pupil's results. There are no goal pages, trackers, class records, mastery logs, progress graphs or mastery gates. *(The screen weighting of §7a is the NAMED exception **EX-MXR-ADAPT** to this rule and to P-RV-9: screen only, never printed, off on teacher links — §9.2.)*
- **P-RV-9** (PEDAGOGY) "Taught" is read from the Teaching sequence list. With no list, the teacher picks the skills for each panel by hand. No pupil data is involved.
- **P-RV-13** (PEDAGOGY) Pages are coded Week and Day in the footer and seeded from that code, so any day can be reprinted exactly.
- **SCC-P14** (CONTRACT) A page role never invents or overrides a skill's options. It receives the configured skill — the id plus its option values — asks it for cells, and lays them out. …
- **SCC-P16** (CONTRACT) Options must survive sharing and saving. A configured skill's option values travel in the settings segment of the share code … A shared code reopens the same configured skill, not the bare id at its defaults. …
- **DN-1** (DESIGN STANDARD) Reference densities above about 40 responses per page were judged too dense for these pupils; outside fact layouts no page exceeds 20 scored responses at L.

## 5. Owner rulings

1. **2026-11-14** — A new paper type plus a playable mode, MIXED REVIEW: any mix of grades (school placement, chips derived, K–6+); any mix of the 9 areas with CCSS domain labels; optional untick of single skills; "Only 8/10 ✓ skills" ON by default, read from `redesign-passed.js`; 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 problems; a seeded random mix with a "New mix" button; every sheet has an answer key. *(owner, relayed by the lead in the lf-mixreview brief)*
2. **2026-11-14** — Built on the EXISTING mixed-practice engine and the review role. No second engine.
3. **2026-11-14** — SENDABLE: a share code / link reproduces the identical mix; it extends the existing share-code systems, append-only.
4. **2026-11-14** — PLAYABLE: practice card, online worksheet, quiz (scored) and the game modes.
5. **2026-11-14** — All five improvements: (1) a Mon–Fri weekly set; (2) spaced / weak-skill weighting on screen; (3) the key and the results tagged by skill, with a per-domain breakdown; (4) order mixed / easy → hard / by area; (5) a "From my lessons" pool.
6. **2026-11-13** — Screens are print, computer / Chromebook 1280–1366 px and tablet 820–1024 px; no 390 px. Print sizes M and L; S dropped (an S setting or code falls back to M). *(CLAUDE.md fastest-implementation plan, items 7 and 9)*
7. **2026-11-19 (lead)** — The 16 open questions are ruled (§9). Ruling 6 changes ruling 1's default: "Only 8/10 ✓" is OFF while the passed pool is small, with a ✓ on every passed skill and the count on the toggle. Ruling 2 names the weighting exception EX-MXR-ADAPT. Ruling 1: `AREA_LABELS` is built by this lane.
8. **2026-11-19 (lead, card round 3, §1.7)** — Root cause of the two failed card critics: a deterministic deal written in prose on top of an engine that measures layout, with nothing executable to prove it. The deal becomes DEALER V1 (`proto/dealer-v1.mjs`) with its machine check (`proto/check-v1.mjs`); the r2 resolutions are §9 ruling 17.

## 6. Misconceptions

| Id | Error | Wrong |
|---|---|---|
| M-MR1 | Carries the last item's procedure into the next (adds on a subtract item after an add item). The interleave is the point, so each cell's own sign and instruction must be visible in the cell (PT-MIX-5 cue), never only in another skill's band strip. | after 34 + 12 = 46, writes 58 − 23 = 81 |
| M-MR2 | Reads difficulty from position (easy → hard) and stops at the first hard one. The default order is mixed; easy → hard is the teacher's choice. | leaves items 7–10 blank |
| M-MR3 | (teacher) Reads one total as mastery. The key summary and the results split the score by area and skill, so a 7 / 10 that is 4 / 4 place value and 0 / 3 time shows as that. | "7 / 10, fine" |

## 7. Options and presets

The options belong to the **page type** (job / section scope, PAGE_TYPES 9), not to any skill. Each dealt skill keeps its own options (SCC-P14): its defaults, or its preset skill's values. No preset skill is added (§9.12).

### 7a. Hosts, roles and options — the decisions (signed)

**Options (the teacher's Mixed review panel)**

| Option | Values | Default | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grades` | chips K, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6+ (multi) and All | the Skills screen's grade selection (`mq_teacher_skills_ui`), else Grade 2 | **offered** — a skill's chips = its **school placement** (the school grades whose pacing lessons link it: `allLessons()` of `wrm-links.js` (rows with `grade`, `seq`, `weeks`) → step → curated `direct` skills + `SKILL_WRM`) ∪ its `data.js` grade; 6+ = grade 6; M skills §9.5; each chip shows its pool count; a 0 chip shows greyed with its count |
| `areas` | 9 chips: CC, OA, NBT, NF, MEAS, DATA, G, RPNS, WORDS | all on | **offered** — from `areaOf`; each chip labelled from `AREA_LABELS` (table below, built by this lane, §9.1); MIXED and NOSTD skills are never in the pool [P:n] |
| `onlyPassed` | on / off | **off** (while the passed pool is small; §9.6) | **offered** — the toggle stays visible with its live count, "Only 8/10 ✓ (32)" = the filtered pool ∩ `REDESIGN_PASSED`; every passed skill in the picker shows a ✓ beside its name whatever the toggle; on = the id is in `REDESIGN_PASSED`, read live [X:MIX-REVIEW-POOL] |
| `skills` (untick) | one tick per pool skill | all ticked | **offered** — stored as the unticked ids, so a skill that joins the pool later arrives ticked |
| `fromLessons` | off / `unit` (this school unit to date) / `4w` (last 4 school weeks) / `year` (school year to date) | off (on → `4w`, §9.11) | **offered** — source in "Lessons pool" below |
| `count` | 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 | 10 | **offered** |

**Share code** (the Direct Play link / enhanced skill code, `?c=<skills>|<tokens>`, `skill-codes.js` `generateEnhancedSkillCode` / `parseEnhancedSkillCode`)

```
?c=AO4-AQ3-AK3|V1-N10-S93CI-Zm                       one sheet, order mixed, size M (pinned: pool-large, S = 424242)
?c=AO4-AQ3-AK7-AN4-…-AA3|V1-N10-S93CI-Oa-Y12-Zm       a Mon-Fri week, week 12, by area (the week's skills with week totals)
?c=<same>|V1-N10-S93CI-Oa-Y12-K3-Zm                   Wednesday of that week
```

- **Skills part:** the DEALT list in the dealer's pick order (`out.dealt`), each part the frozen 2-char code + its item count written as the existing weight digits + its `~options` payload when the skill has options (a single sheet: its counts; a week: the week totals) [P:a]. **The `~options` travel IN the code** (lead ruling 2026-11-20, §9.19): V1's `encode` writes them and `decode` reads them, so the teacher's per-skill choices reproduce on every host [P:a]. Decoding replays the list as the pool, in that order, with no shuffle (`replayInput`), through the FROZEN V1 table (`fixtures/v1-registry.json`: code → id, footprint kind, grade, area; append-only), never the live registry; a code naming a code the table lacks is refused [P:a,i]. The counts are then asserted against the re-deal, never trusted blindly [P:a]. **One codec:** MIX-REVIEW-SHARE `share-two-codecs` (build step 1, a product check) asserts that `skill-codes.js` `generateEnhancedSkillCode` writes, for 100 seeded mixes, the very string `D.encode` writes, byte for byte, `~options` included, and that `parseEnhancedSkillCode` reads back the same skills, counts and options [X:MIX-REVIEW-SHARE].
- **New tokens (appended):** `V1` mixed review, dealer V1 · `S<base36>` the seed · `O<e|a>` order easy → hard / by area (absent = mixed) · `Y<week>` a Mon–Fri week (absent = one sheet) · `K<1–5>` one day of a week code · `P1` adapt to each pupil on screen (absent = off) · **`Z<m|l>` the print size** (r2 N2; Z is free; an `s` reads as m). Reused: `N<n>` count, `G<p|b|r|w>` host, `H`, `T` as today. Letters already taken: T N G R D A Q H W F X. A V1 code without `Z` is refused, and a V1 code without `S` is refused, never read as seed 1 (card r3 D7) [P:a].
- **Why Z:** the page split, the shelves, the M1 rows and so the printed number order depend on the size, through the frozen `CAP` / `SHELF` tables (not through CSS). With Z the code fixes them, and every host plays the list in that order whatever the device [P:a] [X:MIX-REVIEW-HOSTS].
- **Compatibility:** append-only. No frozen code, position or token meaning changes; a code with none of the new tokens decodes byte-for-byte as before (`ws-code-snapshot`, `ws-share-options`) [X:ws-code-snapshot]. An OLD app skips V / S / O / Y / K / P / Z (its `switch` ignores unknown keys) and plays the same skills with the same weights as an ordinary mixed set: the skills survive, the identical items do not. This is stated in the Copy-link panel, not hidden.
- **V1 is four files, frozen by their sha256** (card r3 D1). `V1` means "dealt by `dealer-v1.mjs` with the `js/modules/sheet/interleave.js` (`dealCounts`, `interleave`) and `js/modules/sheet/rng.js` (`rng`, `shuffle`, `deriveSeed`) it imports, over the frozen V1 table `v1-registry.json`", each pinned in `proto/fixtures/frozen.json` [P:i]. Every one of the 20 golden codes of `fixtures/golden-v1.json` (sheets and weeks, three day codes, every N, M and L, every order, filtered pools, a skill with `~options`) replays through the frozen table alone to its pinned pages and items `[n, skill, ~options, seed, page]` [P:i]. So a change to the engine files lf-engine owns, a changed footprint class or grade in the live registry, or a dealer change that keeps its sha, each fails V1 (`fail-i-interleave-edited`, `fail-i-rng-edited`, `fail-i-live-registry`, `fail-i-golden-drift`) [P:i]. The files move to `js/modules/` unchanged at build step 2 (the pins move with them); when lf-engine must change `interleave.js` or `rng.js`, the V1 dealer first gets frozen copies of the two files under `js/modules/mixed-review-v1/` (the pins unchanged), and any change to what V1 deals ships as `V2` in a new file, so every V1 code keeps rebuilding the same sheets and days [P:i]. A week or day code re-runs the frozen week from its skills part; every day code round-trips [P:a]. (Encoding each day's list in the code was rejected: the skills part's `-` grammar has no day separator an old decoder would skip safely.)
- **Identical — one dealer.** The product's `dealReviewItems(req)` (in `print-sheet.js`, beside the duplicate ladder it must run: `RETRIES` = 40 and the rungs unique / answers / turn / repeat) takes the decoded request, calls V1's `deal` / `week` for the PLAN (skills, counts, pages, shelves, numbers, item seeds), and runs each item through `generateQuestionFor` [X:MIX-REVIEW-HOSTS]. **The seeds (card r3 D5):** try 0 of item i is `item.seed` = `deriveSeed('mixed-review', S′, day, i)`, four parts; try r ≥ 1 is `deriveSeed('mixed-review', S′, day, i, r)`, five parts (the two differ: a five-part call with r = 0 is not try 0). S′ is S on a single sheet (day 0), and on day d of a week the day seed `deriveSeed('mixed-review-week', S, d)` (day = d), exactly as V1 seeds them [P:m]. It accepts the first try the ladder passes and returns the ACCEPTED list `[{categoryId, skillId, opts, seed, q}]` in printed order [X:MIX-REVIEW-HOSTS]. `buildSheet` lays out exactly that plan (no measuring decides a page), and every screen host plays exactly that list — none calls `generateQuestionFor` itself — so print and screen match by construction, retries included [X:MIX-REVIEW-HOSTS]. Same code + same release ⇒ byte-identical items [X:MIX-REVIEW-SHARE]. A later release that changes a generator may change numbers; the skills, counts, pages, order and seeds never change under V1 [P:i].
- **Adapt (`P1`).** The pupil's device deals from **the code's listed skills only** (prop g): the weights order the seeded choice among them, the counts are the normal deal. Identical per device, not across pupils.

**Weekly set**

- Five sheets Mon–Fri of N problems each. Day d seed = `deriveSeed('mixed-review-week', S, d)`.
- Rotation (DEALER V1 `week`, frozen with the file): one cycle for the week (`deriveSeed('mixed-review-cycle', S)`); each day deals its sheet with the choice order fresh (unseen this week) → not on yesterday's sheet → least used this sheet → least used this week → pick order. So **every pool skill appears before any repeat other than the planned comeback** (r2 resolution 4), and **no skill falls on two consecutive days** while |pool| ≥ 2·k_d [P:f]. **The comeback:** from Wednesday, the first page of day d opens with the first skill of day d − 2 that is not on day d − 1 (spacing) [P:f]. Prop f exempts exactly that skill on that day [P:f].
- Print: 5 pupil sheets (tab `Week n | Mon` … `Fri`, footer code with K1–K5), then 5 keys, then one weekly key table (PT-KEY-5: areas and skills as rows, Mon–Fri as columns, item numbers in the cells). A pool of exactly 2·k_d skills alternates A / B / A / B / A: each set comes back 2–3 times, no skill falls on consecutive days, and the comeback is then a no-op (r3 open item) [P:f]. Each day reprints exactly from its day code (P-RV-13) [P:a]. The week reuses its one plan for each day; a day code rebuilds that same day, never re-plans it differently (L24) [P:a].

**Weighting** (screen only, `adapt` on) — **EX-MXR-ADAPT, the named screen-only exception to PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9** (owner request 2026-11-14; §9.2): never printed, never sent, never a teacher record, off on teacher links unless "Adapt to each pupil" (`P1`) [X:MIX-REVIEW-POOL].

- w(skill) = 1 + due + weak. due = 1 when `state.spacedRepetition[skillId].nextReview` ≤ today (+1 more at Leitner box 1 or 2); weak = 1 when `state.skillProgress[skillId].total` ≥ 5 and `mastery` < 70; a skill with no record has w = 1; w ∈ 1..4.
- **The pool is the code's listed skills only** (r2 resolution 7): adapt never reads the filters or the full pool [P:g]. w orders the seeded choice among them (V1 `weightedOrder`, keys u^(1/w)); the per-skill counts are the §2 deal unchanged (even on each page, at most ceil(N / 2)); w never reaches `dealCounts` [P:g].
- **A pupil-started mix** (the pupil's own "Mixed review" button) has no picker: it starts from the last teacher code opened on that device — its listed skills, N, order and size, i.e. the teacher-set filters as the teacher dealt them, carried in the code — with adapt on. With no saved teacher code the button is not offered.
- Read once at start (a snapshot): the session's list is fixed. Results go back through the `updateSkillProgress` / `updateSpacedRepetition` path every host already calls [X:MIX-REVIEW-HOSTS]. Never on print, never sent, never a teacher record (EX-MXR-ADAPT, §9.2) [X:MIX-REVIEW-POOL]. Keyed by bare `skillId`, as `progress.js` keys it today.

**Breakdown layout** (key and results)

- **Key summary** (teacher page; Andika, black and white; 11 / 12 pt at M / L): columns **Area** (name + CCSS domain code) | **Skill** (label) | **Items** (numbers) | **Score ___ / n**; one subtotal row per area `___ / n_area`, in `AREA_ORDER`; a total row `___ / N`. Under the last key page's grid when its rows fit, else its own key page. Built from `skillItemMap(plan)` + `areaOf`.
- **Results** (online-worksheet score card, quiz results, the game end screen): "By area" rows (area name + icon; screen chrome may use the area colour, PT-SCR-1) with correct / total and the item numbers, each opening to its skills, weakest first. The quiz results extend the existing `skillAnalysis` (quiz-results.js) with the area grouping; the game end screen reads `game-flow.js`'s `skillBreakdown`.
- Per-skill and per-area subtotals always sum to N [X:MIX-REVIEW-BREAKDOWN].

**Order modes**

- `mixed`: V1 §2 Order — the M1 item interleave on a one-class page, seeded shelf order otherwise; no avoidable adjacent pair, a single-skill page exempt (prop d). The M2 block packer is not needed (§9.4). There is no separate screen order: the hosts play the printed order.
- `easyhard`: shelves by placement grade, then pick order (on each page).
- `area`: `AREA_ORDER`, then placement grade (on each page).
- Numbering 1..N row-major on paper; every screen host plays the items in the printed number order, so item 7 is the same problem everywhere [X:MIX-REVIEW-HOSTS].

**Lessons pool** (`fromLessons` on)

- For each ticked grade g: the lessons of g's school sequence (`allLessons()` from `wrm-links.js`, the rows with `grade` = g, `seq` and `weeks`; `unitLessons(g, unit)` for the `unit` window) whose week lies in the window ending at `weekForDate(g, today)` → their WRM steps → the skills listed `direct` for those steps in `data/curriculum/links/<YEAR>.json`, plus `skillsForWrmStep(step)` (`SKILL_WRM`).
- Then the area, only-8/10 and untick filters apply as usual.
- Outside the school year (no week): `year` = the whole sequence; `unit` / `4w` say "No school week today" and fall back to `year`.
- No pupil data and no teacher records (P-RV-9).

The `labels` assert of step 1b: `AREA_LABELS` deep-equals the §7a table (11 keys, exact strings), and **no file outside `teacher-areas.js` holds the whole map** (a file containing all 11 label strings); single area words elsewhere are allowed (r2 resolution 5). | — (browser + a node assert) | an item missing from the summary or listed twice → `breakdown-dup-item` · an item under the wrong area → `breakdown-wrong-area` · subtotals that do not sum → `breakdown-sum` · a results screen whose numbers differ from the key's → `breakdown-screen-differs` · an `AREA_LABELS` entry that differs from §7a → `labels-changed` · a second whole label map in another file → `labels-second-map` |

## 9. Rulings (lead, 2026-11-19)

The lead ruled on the 16 open questions on 2026-11-19 (via the coordinator). Each question is kept with its ruling.

1. **AREA_LABELS is not in the repo (lf-checks has not added it; teacher-areas.js has AREA_ORDER / AREAS with 8 maths areas + MIXED, WORDS, NOSTD). Which are the 9 areas and their CCSS domain labels?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): AREA_LABELS is ours to build: a new export of js/modules/teacher-areas.js with the exact labels of the lessons-browser card (card areaLabels); build-plan step 1b. The 9 pool areas are the 8 maths areas + WORDS; MIXED and NOSTD never in the pool. lf-checks reuses ours.
2. **Weak-skill weighting reads the pupil's own progress, which PT-DLG-26 and P-RV-9 forbid for pages. Allow it on screen?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): The weak-skill weighting is the NAMED screen-only exception EX-MXR-ADAPT to PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9, because the owner asked for it: the pupil's own device record, a start-of-session snapshot, never printed, never sent, never a teacher record, off on teacher links unless 'Adapt to each pupil' (P1). Named in PT-MXR-9 and in the PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9 amendment sentences.
3. **Role id: a ROLE_ALIASES entry mixed-review -> mixed-practice with input.review, or a thin roles/mixed-review.js wrapper?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): Role id: a ROLE_ALIASES entry mixed-review -> mixed-practice with input.review (title, tab, supports level 1, exact total, order, fill off); no new module.
4. **Order 'mixed' when the dealt skills have different size classes (the usual case across grades and areas): the M2 2 x 2 block packer is not built.** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): Order mixed across size classes: a shelf-level interleave (each shelf one skill with its band strip, shelf order seeded, no two shelves of one skill adjacent); the M1 interleaved shelves for one size class; M2 later, no format change.
5. **Grade 'M' (Mixed levels) skills, e.g. the two vocabulary skills, and the 6+ chip: where do they sit?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): Grade M skills sit under every chip their school placement lists, else under every ticked chip (counted once). 6+ = grade 6 skills.
6. **The only-8/10 pool is small: 32 skills, all OA / NBT / Words (grade 4: 1 skill, grade 6+: none). With the default ON most area chips are empty.** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): 'Only 8/10 ✓ skills' defaults OFF while the passed pool is small. Every passed skill shows a ✓ in the picker; the toggle stays visible with its count, e.g. 'Only 8/10 ✓ (32)'. A pool under 2 skills is refused with its reason; never widened silently.
7. **N = 5 is a short page (about 40 % at L): H5 says a page under half used is wasted.** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead; wording corrected after card critic r1, D12): N = 5 prints 2-up when the 5 items fit a half page (M typical / compact, L compact): the same 5 items twice on one sheet with a dashed cut line, each half with its own header, numbered 1–5 and scored /5, the key 2-up the same way. Otherwise the §3 table's pages apply.
8. **Per-skill options inside a mix (a teacher who wants mult_facts 7s and 8s only).** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): Per-skill options in v1: each skill at its defaults or its preset's values; the code already carries ~opts.
9. **Week sharing: one week link with a day picker, or five day links?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): Week sharing: one week link (Y) that opens a day picker; the Copy menu also gives each day's link (K).
10. **Quiz host: a new G letter, or the existing quiz builder and ?quiz= share?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): Quiz host: 'Make a quiz' builds a one-section quiz of the mix's N items (each tagged with its skill), shared with the existing ?quiz=; no new G letter.
11. **From my lessons: the default window when the teacher turns it on, and is the school pacing the right source (not the teacher's own plan)?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): From my lessons: default window '4w' when turned on; source = the school pacing (P-RV-9).
12. **Does the owner rule 'a distinct option is also a findable skill' apply?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): No preset skill and no new tags: mixed review is a page type, findable as 'mixed review', 'spiral review', 'review sheet' in the print picker.
13. **Should the pupil page name the area (band titles 'Place value', 'Time')?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): The pupil page never names the area: instruction strips only; the key summary, footer CCSS codes and results name them.
14. **May the teacher turn the key off?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): The key print may be unticked (default on); it is always built, previewed and reachable from the code (PT-KEY-1).
15. **Defaults: 10 problems, order mixed, size = the teacher's print default (L when unset), week off, fromLessons off?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): Defaults: 10 problems, order mixed, size = the teacher's print default (L when unset), week off, from my lessons off, only 8/10 off.
16. **Signing: ws-spec-card has no page-type kind, so this card has no machine block and --check-signed cannot verify it.** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead): The card stays hand-written (kind page-type) and is signed by hand; lane MR-E may later add a page-type kind to ws-spec-card and regenerate it.

17. **Card critic r2 (FAIL, min 6): how are its findings resolved?** Ruling (2026-11-19, lead, card round 3): (1) a single-skill wide page is exempt from adjacency; (2) the deal is a pure dealer with a frozen size × footprint page table and a `Z<m|l>` size token; (3) a skill's short last shelf is allowed (H13 measures inside cells); (4) the comeback is exempt from "before any repeat"; (5) the `AREA_LABELS` assert: no other file holds the WHOLE label map; (6) one named fixture per FAIL state for every check; (7) adapt samples only the code's listed skills, and a pupil-started mix uses the teacher-set filters carried in the code; (8) boss and race end at N, scored out of N; (9) cite `allLessons()`, not LESSONS.

18. **H5 on pools that mix wide and flat skills (round 3 open item): may a page be under half full?** Ruling (2026-11-20, lead): (a) the LAST page of an exact-N sheet may be under half full, because the teacher chose N; (b) whenever a class page (wide or flat) would be under half full, wide and flat items share ONE page by fill (each item 1 / C of its class's cap, the sum ≤ 1), keeping at most 3 skills a page, no avoidable adjacency, ceil(N / 2), the shelves and determinism. Proved by `check-v1` property k and `--fill`.

19. **The `~options` suffix (card critic r3 defect 8): in the code, or dropped from the card?** Ruling (2026-11-20, lead, card round 4): the `~options` suffix travels IN the code, so the teacher's per-skill choices reproduce. The prototype's `encode` writes it after each part's count and `decode` reads it (check-v1 prop a, FAIL `fail-a-drop-opts`); the card states it one way (§7a Skills part). MIX-REVIEW-SHARE `share-two-codecs` (build step 1, a product check) asserts that `skill-codes.js` `generateEnhancedSkillCode` output equals `D.encode` byte for byte, `~options` included.

20. **Card critic r3 (FAIL, min 6): root cause and resolution.** Ruling (2026-11-20, lead, card round 4, the final root-cause round): the class of r2 and r3 is "the card states a normative deal rule no property asserts". Every normative sentence of §2, §3, §7a and the PT-MXR rules carries a property tag, and `check-v1.mjs --trace` (in its default run) fails on any without one, or with one naming nothing. The eight r3 defects are fixed in §9e, each with a property and a FAIL fixture.

|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Share-code replay re-deals a DIFFERENT sheet on about 0.5 % of codes (501 of 108,000 single sheets; up to 17 % on kind pools): replay deals from the dealt list alone, so the dealer chooses with a smaller cycle | **MR-SHARE-EXACT** (new step after step 5): `deal()` returns the replay of its own code (deal -> encode -> replay, one pass); until it lands the share UI shows NO warning to teachers (owner ruling) | `deal(replay(code(x))) == deal(x)` swept in `check-v1 --fill` and in MIX-REVIEW-SHARE, FAIL fixture `fail-a-replay-drift` |

## 7b. What the repo offers today (informational, not signed)

Read by hand from the repo on 2026-11-19 (master d3830882). Not part of the signed card.

**Page roles (`print-sheet.js` SHEET_ROLES + `sheet/roles/index.js` ROLE_MODULES / ROLE_ALIASES):** independent, more-practice, opener (lesson-opener), scripted-model (model), guided, error-analysis (check-it), review, test (test-a, test-b), pre-skill-check (pre-skill), word-problems, fact-rows, fact-probe, mixed-practice (mixed), true-false, reason-it (reason), stretch, lesson; answer-key is the companion of all. No `mixed-review` yet. The teacher picker (`teacher-print.js` PAGE_TYPES) lists "Mixed review: Mixed practice · Daily 4 · Daily spiral · Today's Number"; only Mixed practice is WORKING.

**Mixed practice today:** GROUPED shelves (PT-MIX-4) and the M1 mixed arrangement for one size class (`mixedClass`, `interleave`, `dealCounts` min 2); the count FILLS the page (`total = shelves × k`), with `fill` off (`F0`) for a short page; the M2 block packer for mixed size classes is not built.

**Screen hosts the screen gates drive:** practice-card, online-worksheet, quiz, boss, race, map, mode-dark, mode-bigboard.

**Share-code settings tokens in use** (`generateEnhancedSkillCode`): T timer, N count, G mode (p b r w), R range, D decimals, A adaptive, Q Quick Start lock, H help, W arrangement (m p), F fill, X related facts. Skill parts: 2-char code + weight digits + `~options`.

**Pool sources:** `REDESIGN_PASSED` 32 ids (2026-11-19); `teacher-areas.js` `AREA_ORDER` (CC OA NBT NF MEAS DATA G RPNS MIXED WORDS NOSTD) — no `AREA_LABELS`; school pacing in `wrm-links.js` (`allLessons()`, `unitLessons()`, `schoolWeeksOf`, `weekForDate`), grades PK–5 (WRM R, Y1–Y6); progress `state.skillProgress` and `state.spacedRepetition` keyed by bare skill id.

**Results today:** `quiz-results.js` groups by skill (`skillAnalysis`, weakest first); `game-flow.js` saves `skillBreakdown` per session; `answer-key.js` has `skillItemMap` and `answerListRows`. No area grouping anywhere yet.
